honesty_rule: The human reviewer's rates are inputs. A single simulation run can only show what follows if reviewers behave as the cited studies measured. The break-even sweep shows how far reviewer behaviour would have to move before the conclusion flips.

catch.source: Edmundson et al. 2013, ESSoS: 30 reviewers, 7 known vulnerabilities, mean 2.33 found; 2.33 / 7

false_flag_ratio.source: Edmundson et al. 2013: mean 6.29 reported, 2.33 correct; (6.29 - 2.33) / 2.33 (derived)

false_reject.source: derived per run: 1.70 x catch x p_imperm / (1 - p_imperm), p_imperm the arm's share of impermissible changes reaching review

rework_minutes.source: assumption: rework after a false reject

flat-edmundson.source: primary model: sourced or directly derived values only

braz-unprompted.source: Braz et al. 2022, ICSE: unprompted reviewers found 3% and 21% of two injected flaws; mean 0.12

braz-prompted.source: Braz et al. 2022: a security focus raised detection about eight-fold; min(1, 0.12 x 8). Upper sensitivity only

visibility.source: assumption: what a reviewer can only see by consulting records, precedent, a second rule or the evidence is caught less often

crunch.source: assumption: lighter review under schedule pressure

no-false-flags.source: the most favourable human: no wasted blocks

sample_per_quarter.source: assumption, in the range typically sampled for a change-management control

rulebook.source: assumption on an order-of-magnitude scale: absolute 100; binding citation with a legal, regulatory or safety harm 20; internal standard with such a harm 5; else 1; VAL-ACC 20

sources: Edmundson, A., Holtkamp, B., Rivera, E., Finifter, M., Mettler, A., Wagner, D. (2013). An empirical study on the effectiveness of security code review. ESSoS 2013.
Braz, L., Aeberhard, C., Calikli, G., Bacchelli, A. (2022). Less is more: supporting developers in vulnerability detection during code review. ICSE 2022. arXiv 2202.04586.
